title: Direct ab initio calculation of magnons in altermagnets: method, spin-space symmetry aspects, and application to MnTe
method: DFT (LDA) with two constraints (magnetization-change constraint + generalized-translation/symmetry constraint fixing the magnon wave vector) to compute adiabatic magnons directly; analysis via spin-space groups (SSG). We do NOT reproduce the full DFT; we build a from-scratch minimal tight-binding altermagnet surrogate of alpha-MnTe to test the electronic-structure headline claim.
model_system: alpha-MnTe, NiAs-type hexagonal structure (a=4.15 A, c=6.71 A). Two Mn sublattices (A,B) with antiparallel collinear moments, related by a spin-space-group operation combining a real-space rotation (C6z-type screw) with spin flip -- NOT by translation or inversion. Nonmagnetic Te atoms make the two Mn local environments rotated copies -> altermagnetism.

key_params.sublattice_connecting_op: C6z-type rotation + spin reversal (SSG type-II op includes mirror-z which reverses spin => splitting odd in kz)

headline_claim: alpha-MnTe is an altermagnet: the collinear antiparallel Mn sublattices give ZERO net magnetic moment, yet the electron states show a nonzero, momentum-dependent altermagnetic SPIN SPLITTING DeltaE(k)=E_up(k)-E_down(k). This splitting is ZERO on the high-symmetry line (0,0,kz) (spin degeneracy protected), NONZERO at general k (e.g. (0.1,0.2,kz)), and has a sign-changing g-wave symmetry pattern (nodal planes; BZ integral of the splitting = 0), identical in reciprocal-space pattern to the magnon chirality splitting.
testable_predictions: P1: net spin moment integrated over BZ ~ 0 (compensated antiferromagnet)
P2: spin splitting DeltaE(0,0,kz) = 0 along the high-symmetry line
P3: spin splitting DeltaE != 0 at a general k such as (0.1,0.2,kz)
P4: DeltaE(k) changes sign under the sublattice-connecting rotation -> BZ-average of DeltaE = 0, with a multi-lobe (d/g-wave) nodal pattern (NOT s-wave / ferromagnetic uniform splitting)
P5: DeltaE is odd under kz -> -kz (type-II mirror-z spin reversal)
